 De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Suns. 
 A late addition to the Kings’ injury report, Hunter did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. Dylan Cardwell replaced him in the starting lineup, with Keegan Murray moving to small forward. Expect the same on Wednesday if Hunter can’t play. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray and Domantas Sabonis will start Wednesday’s game against the Suns. 
 After missing Sunday’s loss to the Thunder, LaVine and Hunter are back in the Kings’ starting lineup. As a result, Malik Monk and Dylan Cardwell will come off the bench. The other three starters are unchanged.

 De’Andre Hunter (hip) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns. 
 Hunter missed Sunday’s loss to the Thunder with a hip injury. Dylan Cardwell will likely head back to the bench with Hunter returning to the starting lineup Wednesday against the Suns.

 Darius Acuff Jr., Malik Monk, Keegan Murray, Dylan Cardwell and Domantas Sabonis will start Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 The Kings are without Zach LaVine and De’Andre Hunter, opening up two spots in the starting lineup. Monk and Cardwell will fill the resulting voids, making both players worth streaming in deep leagues.

 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Add Hunter’s name to the list of Kings contributors who won’t be available for Sunday’s game. With Precious Achiuwa also out, Leaky Black could move into the starting lineup. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Hunter is a late addition to the Kings’ injury report, which generally doesn’t bode well for his availability. With Precious Achiuwa (ankle) out, Leaky Black could see his playing time increase, even if he isn’t inserted into the starting lineup. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter scored 24 points (7-of-13 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, and two 3-pointers in 41 minutes in loss to Blazers. 
 The Kings needed the offense in this one with Darius Acuff having a down game, and Hunter gave them some solid offense. He got the line a lot in this game which is a rarity. This isn’t a sign to add De’Andre Hunter, but it’s more of a reminder that he can be useful as a points streamer if your schedule permits it. 
 Maxime Raynaud 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #42 
 Kings insider James Ham reports that Maxime Raynaud (knee) is progressing but has no official timeline to return. 
 The backup big man has yet to make his season debut, but until he returns, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa should continue to pickup the slack in the frontcourt. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa (leg) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Magic with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench. Keegan Murray (11/2/1 with four blocks and two three-pointers) played 24 minutes as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury. 
 Maxime Raynaud 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #42 
 Maxime Raynaud (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic. 
 Working his way back from a right patellar subluxation suffered during the preseason, Raynaud was to be re-evaluated early this week. That did not happen on Monday, but the Kings are listing the second-year center out for Tuesday night. Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell have been providing depth at center when Domantas Sabonis is not on the floor. 
 Dylan Cardwell 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #32 
 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury.

 Davion Mitchell had 24 points (8-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, one block and six three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 Mitchell’s run of excellent play continued against the Bucks Wednesday. The 28-year-old guard is averaging 19.3 points, 9.9 assists and 3.4 rebounds while shooting 52.3 percent from the field and 46.8 percent from behind the three-point line over his last seven games. Mitchell is turning out to be one of the biggest steals of the fantasy basketball season and should receive consideration for the All-Star team.
